summary: Core IAM→PR/merge→deliver→webhook path is real, coupled, and non-toy via ccctl, but the package fails large_system_strict Q6: honest non-seed runtime/config LOC is ~2,859 (~2,875 with schema.sql), below the >=3,000 floor; ~1,350 LOC of admin/report fan-out is explicitly framed as LOC-floor padding; 24 team-fragment policies are clones; and bin/cc-api serve() returns an unbound httpd so one primary entrypoint is not runtime-reachable.

evidence.observation: Q6 independently judges whether the solver-visible core is complex, reachable, coupled, non-toy, and non-padded. For large_system_strict, >=3,000 substantive reachable runtime/config LOC is necessary but not sufficient; Complexity Governor or authenticity-validator PASS is not enough.

Q6 method requires entrypoint tracing, reachability, distinct module responsibilities, clone/wrapper/padding checks, cross-module invariants, a ~25% removal test, and separating production logic from generated/config/data noise. PASS needs >=3,000 substantive reachable LOC and no HIGH toy/padding risk.

Count only implementation that materially participates in the claimed operational system. Dead/unreachable/unnecessary code and construction toward the 3,000-LOC floor via filler are authenticity defects. Seed volume is not authored runtime complexity.

findings.criterion: large_system_strict requires >=3000 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC
evidence_refs: static LOC inventory over environment/codecommit/lib/**/*.py excl. seed.py
findings.why_it_matters: Even counting nearly all non-seed Python plus schema.sql, the package sits ~2,859–2,875 LOC—below the strict floor. Seed warehouse rows and seed.py are not runtime/config logic.
findings.minimal_remediation: Deepen material control-plane behavior (IAM/git/PR/pipeline/webhook/state) until honest substantive reachable runtime/config LOC clears 3000 without filler modules or cloned config.
findings.regression_risk: Adding more reporting wrappers or duplicate policies to chase the number will worsen padding findings without fixing authenticity.

findings.criterion: complexity must come from domain invariants/state transitions, not chores or padding toward the LOC floor; no HIGH padding risk for PASS
findings.why_it_matters: operator_workflows explicitly admits LOC-floor padding; platform-job fans into large admin/report modules (~1.3k LOC) whose removal would not erase the IAM/merge/deliver contract; 24 team-fragment policies are one cloned template. That is HIGH padding risk and blocks PASS even if raw LOC later crosses 3000.
findings.minimal_remediation: Remove or replace floor-padding modules/cloned fragments with differentiated, load-bearing control-plane behavior reached from normal operator workflows—not a nightly LOC aggregator.
findings.regression_risk: Deleting padding without deepening the core will leave the LOC floor unmet; keep the coupled IAM/merge/deliver path intact.

findings.criterion: major modules/entrypoints must be reachable from real operator workflows
findings.why_it_matters: Documented primary HTTP entrypoint cannot start: serve() returns unbound httpd after assigning only Handler.httpd, and never applies the fixed flag. That is a reachability defect for half of the claimed operator surface.
findings.minimal_remediation: Fix serve() to construct/bind httpd, set Handler.fixed, and return the live server so cc-api matches the contract.
findings.regression_risk: Low if limited to serve() wiring; do not weaken IAM/merge defects while repairing reachability.

findings.criterion: business/runtime modules should contain material branching and cross-component interactions
findings.why_it_matters: The non-padded core is credible production logic with partial-fix traps across IAM, quorum, FF merge, deliver dedupe, and outbox. This is advisory context: the task is not purely toy; scale/padding/API reachability still block PASS.
findings.minimal_remediation: Preserve and deepen this coupled core while removing padding; do not replace it with more report wrappers.
